svg.title: Framework for reading a market-making backtest
svg.desc: A five-step ladder shows net PnL, activity, inventory and execution quality, robustness, and locked out-of-sample evaluation.

g.text: How I read a market-making backtest
A result advances only when it survives every layer below. No single metric is a performance verdict.
Are fees, rebates, marking and exit costs already included?
Gross spread capture is not the result.
How many trades, how much notional and how much time in market?
A small loss can simply mean that the strategy did almost nothing.
What happens after fills, and can the assumed fills be trusted?
Inspect markout, inventory tails, queue assumptions, latency and partial fills.
Does the worst fold survive? Does a deflated Sharpe check pass?
An unusually smooth result is a reason to audit the model, not celebrate it.
Was the final test truly unavailable during research?
Only then is it a final evaluation rather than another selection fold.
The relative weights can vary by strategy and venue. This is the conservative baseline I use before a result is called promising.
